{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study performs a quantitative comparison of multiple murine models against human clinical outcomes for MASLD, developing a 'human proximity score' (MHPS) to rank models based on their concordance with human disease features. This directly measures agreement between animal model results and human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "methods-and-bias",
  "arm_evidence": "We developed a bioinformatic pipeline integrating metabolic phenotype data, liver histology (with centralized staining and assessment) and liver transcriptome benchmarked against human disease to create a MASLD ‘human proximity score’ (MHPS; Fig. 1).",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "hepatic",
    "metabolic"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Main Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is the hepatic manifestation of the metabolic syndrome 1.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "We collected retrospective information from 598 animals (509 WT/GA mice, 89 WT/GA rats): 336 animals subjected to treatment (MASLD-inducing conditions: 315 animals; or CCl 4 : 21 animals) and 262 animals as controls for MASLD-inducing conditions (247 animals) or CCl 4 (15 animals), returning 39 models (that is, study designs) aimed at modeling MASLD...",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "We collected retrospective information from 598 animals (509 WT/GA mice, 89 WT/GA rats)...",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The MHPS system ranks murine models based on their congruence with human MASLD in terms of metabolic (illustrated in Fig. 6a ; details in Extended Data Figure 3 ) and/or fibro-inflammatory (shown in Fig. 6b ; details in Extended Data Figure 4 ) profiles."
}
